title: Caching: remember the answer, beware stale
intro: Asking the database is slow. A cache keeps answers close by, but what if the answer changes?

predict.question: Ann is renamed to Anna in the database, but the cache still holds her. What does the next cache read return?
options: An error, because the data changed
predict.reveal: The cache has no idea the database changed. It returns Ann until the entry expires or the app deletes it.

takeaway: A cache trades freshness for speed: reads get much faster, so you must expire or invalidate entries when data changes.

steps.say: The app needs user 42's profile. The cache, a fast memory store, is empty. The database is slow but has the truth.
The app asks the cache first for user 42.
Nothing there yet. That is a cache miss.
On a miss the app falls back to the database.
The database finds Ann, but it took about 80 ms.
The app saves the answer in the cache with a TTL (time to live) of 60 seconds, so it expires on its own.
Next request: ask the cache again.
A cache hit! The answer comes back in about 1 ms and the database is never bothered.
Now Ann changes her name. The database says Anna, but the cache still holds Ann.
The next read is a hit, but it is stale: the cache serves the old name. Fast and wrong.
Fix: when the app updates the user, it also deletes the cache key. This is invalidation.
The next read misses, reloads Anna from the database, and caches it. TTL expiry would heal it too, just later.
